newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan opposition leader dies after car accident.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan opposition leader dies after car accident.

text.p: Veteran Moroccan politician Ali Yata died overnight from injuries suffered in a car accident at the weekend, the official Moroccan news agency MAP said on Wednesday.
Yata, 76, was secretary-general of the Progress and Socialism Party (PPS), one of four parties in the opposition Koutla bloc. His party held 14 seats in the 333-seat parliament.
The veteran politician started his political career with the Moroccan Communist Party -- when Morocco was under French protectorate -- which was later banned.
His political activities earned him several prison terms and expulsion from the country.
After the banning of the Communist Party, Yata joined the Party for Liberation and Socialism until it too was banned.
Yata founded and ran several newspapers, and at the time of his death was director of the PPS daily newspaper Al Bayane.
MAP said that Yata had suffered a serious head injury and multiple fractures in the accident last Saturday when he was caught between two parked cars as a third crashed into one.
His funeral is to be held on Thursday in Morocco's financial centre, Casablanca.
Yata was married with four children.
